source: can you make a 1v1v1v1v1v1 first person 3d game about who can find the exit first in the arcade? In the arcade there will be rooms hinting or tricking you into finding the exit! who ever finds it last loses! The game also has multiple maps ( you can decide on what they are going to be ) and everyone has to decide which map they want to play!

image_prompt.text: Corridors between the arcade rooms that circle back on themselves, so a wrong turn costs a detour rather than a long backtrack
Feature walls in each room placed in the player's natural first-person camera path, carrying hints toward the exit - and in some rooms, hints that point the wrong way
A lobby where the six players gather and pick which map to play before the round starts
The exit door itself, visually distinct enough to recognise the moment it is found
Rooms built to mislead - dead-end arcades, false exits, doors that loop back to somewhere already visited
Arcade dressing throughout: cabinets, neon signage, prize counters, patterned carpet
Three map variants on the same maze principle - a retro pixel-art arcade, a futuristic holographic arcade, and a carnival arcade with booths

layout_placement.text: Key items the maze's solve inputs are waiting for
Six start points spread evenly through the maze so no player begins closer to the exit than another
A win trigger on the exit that records finishing order - first out wins, last out loses

notes: Multiple maps are genuinely separate spaces and should carry P4, but P4 lives on the Party & Casual space-staged shape row and the dominant genre owns the shape, so it is flagged here rather than routed.
The maze route is P6 - topology generated first and dressed as an arcade afterward - which matters here because a maze with an unreachable exit would break the only win condition the game has.
The user delegated map choice to us ('you can decide what they are going to be'), so the three variants above are our invention, not theirs.
The competitive framing is a race, but the content is a maze puzzle; Puzzle was taken as dominant because the rooms and their misleading clues are what the sentence is about.

open_questions.ask: How long should a round last - is finding the exit a minute of searching, or five?
Does the round end when the first player is out, or does everyone keep going until only the loser is left inside?

theme: Arcade neon - cabinets, blacklight glow, patterned carpet and prize counters; nearest listed vocabulary is Sci-Fi / Cyberpunk for the neon, but arcade is taken as written

coverage_missing.ask: Does the round stop at the first finisher, or run until only one player is left?
How big is one arcade - a dozen rooms, or fifty?
You left the maps to us; do you want them all arcade-flavoured, or should they range further?
Are there collectibles or keys in the maze, or is the exit found purely by navigation?

answers.ask: How long should a round last - is finding the exit a minute of searching, or five?
answers.answer: Make each round a quick one-minute search so the game stays fast and replayable.

answers.ask: Does the round end when the first player is out, or does everyone keep going until only the loser is left inside?
answers.answer: Everyone keeps going after finding the exit; the round ends once only the last player is still inside, and that player loses.
